storyBlocks.text: A Happy People seminar is not an afternoon where you lean back and try to stay awake for three hours. You take part.
We talk with each other, we laugh, we listen, we ask questions — and sometimes we come across topics you may never have really paused to consider.
Psychology, spirituality, archaeology, history, human beliefs and personal stories come together. Not to tell you what to believe, but to explore together.
Because I believe things get interesting the moment you dare to say:
‘Maybe I don’t know.’
That is where curiosity begins for me.
Why do people think the way they think? Where do our beliefs come from? How much of what we take for granted have we actually examined for ourselves?
And when we look beyond our daily lives, very different questions suddenly arise.

How were the Nazca Lines created? How did people build the pyramids of Giza thousands of years ago? What do we really know about civilisations that disappeared? And what might we still learn from the seven wonders of the ancient world?
We also look at ancient traditions such as Jainism, with ideas about karma, non-violence and the realisation that reality may have more sides than we can see from our own perspective.
And perhaps along the way we arrive at a question once posed by Erich von Däniken:
‘Were the gods astronauts?’
Not to convince you of it, but to make you pause at the question:
How do we actually know what we think we know?
That, for me, is the heart of it.
During a Happy People seminar you do not have to believe in anything. You do not have to reject anything either.
You may be Catholic, Muslim, Buddhist, Jewish, Christian, agnostic, atheist — or simply someone who says: I don’t know, but I want to explore.
Everything is welcome on the table.
Perhaps we discover that despite all our differences, we have much more in common than we think.
That behind different religions and worldviews, the same human questions keep appearing.
Who are we? Why are we here? How do we want to live? And what actually connects us to one another?
And perhaps the Jain idea that you never see the whole story from one perspective is a beautiful key to looking at this.
Not choosing between all or nothing, but daring to listen to what another perspective can teach you.
One plus one does not always have to equal two.
Sometimes something new emerges when you place two perspectives side by side.
Perhaps that is part of the missing link we are all searching for: not another belief that must replace the other, but the ability to truly understand one another.
And that perhaps fits Happy People best.
More than just listening.

eventBlocks.text: IDENTITY · CONNECTION · MANIFESTATION
Who are you when you let go of other people’s expectations for a moment?
Which patterns sometimes quietly shape your choices?
And what happens when your thoughts, words and actions point in the same direction again?
You will not get ready-made answers.
You get something else: the space to look for yourself.
To ask questions. To share experiences. To listen. And to discover new possibilities.
You do not need to know exactly what you are looking for. You do not need a plan. Just come as you are.
Maybe you recognise a pattern you have been stuck in for a while. Maybe an unexpected insight arises. Or maybe you simply go home with a good conversation and a head full of new thoughts.
That counts too.
WHAT CAN YOU EXPECT?

items: practical insights on identity, relationships and beliefs
a chance to meet other participants

eventBlocks.text: You do not come only to listen. You come to take part, think along and set something in motion.
The number of places is deliberately limited. Not to seem exclusive. But because personal attention works better when you are not sitting in a hall with a thousand people at once.

Maybe it is not about becoming someone else in the end.
Maybe it is about rediscovering who you already were.
Give yourself the space to look at that calmly.
Maybe your journey begins here.
